rationale: Variant orthography of ⲡⲓⲱⲱⲃⲉ on root ⲱⲱⲃⲉ 'transgress' (in glossary). The ⲯ-onset may reflect a graphical convention or reduction of ⲡ̄ⲱ. Paired with ⲡϯⲧⲕⲉⲥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'sting of the soul' as the moral-psychological pair the catechumen's hands guard against.

Recurring noun lines 12-14 in clearly devotional context: 'they go to ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲛ daily, every hour' and 'all the hours of [ⲱⲗ]ⲏⲛ.' Likely Lycopolitan reduction of Greek προσευχή 'prayer' or related devotional-liturgical term. Distinct from accumulated ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲗ 'the prayer' (= ϣⲗⲏⲗ); ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲛ may be a parallel formation or scribal variant.

Compound ⲡⲉϩ- ('his') + ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲛ̄ⲕⲁⲧⲉ ('sleep'). The catechumen 'purifies his sleeping-place' — i.e., abstains from sexual relations during the Sunday fast. Direct designation of the marriage-bed as a locus of ritual purification.

proposed_english: share in / take part in (lit. 'do the half-portion')
rationale: Verbal idiom: ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲡⲧⲡⲉϣⲉ ('the half-share'). The catechumens 'share in' the apostolic work of refining the Living Soul. Distinct from the homophone ⲡⲉϣⲉ used cosmologically; here it is the participatory share-portion of soteriological labor.
Greek ἀκμήν 'still, even now, namely.' Discourse-marker introducing specification: 'the other half regarding sins, namely the sins which he habitually commits.'
Greek πιστός 'faithful, believer.' Standard Christian-Manichaean technical term for those who hold the faith — here qualifying the catechumens (the lay faithful as opposed to the elect).

Recurring noun lines 20-22 dividing the year structurally: ⲡⲧⲡⲉϣⲉ 'his half (of fast)' / ⲧⲕⲉⲡⲡⲉϣⲉ 'the other half (of sins)' / ⲛ̄ⲧⲧⲉϣⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲣⲁⲙⲡⲉ 'in the half of the year.' From ⲡⲱϣ 'divide.' Provides the binary mathematical frame for the kephalaion's reckoning of merit.

Greek παρατήρησις 'observance, watchful keeping' (cf. Luke 17:20) with Lyc. ⲍ/ϩ-onset assimilated to preposition ⲍⲛ̄. Devotional-disciplinary register for the catechumen's attentive maintenance of prayer-hours.
